'''The NEXT: Museum, Library, and Preservation Space''' is a repository of [[electronic literature]]. It is supported by  [[Washington State University Vancouver|Washington State University at Vancouver]] and the [[Electronic Literature Organization]].<ref name=wsu>{{cite web|url=https://cas.wsu.edu/2021/09/02/students-create-virtual-museum-of-digital-literature/|title=Students create virtual museum of digital literature|publisher=WSU|date=2021-09-02|accessdate=2024-02-26 |language=}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.vancouver.wsu.edu/news/wsu-vancouver-students-create-virtual-museum-digital-literature|title=WSU Vancouver students create virtual museum of digital literature |publisher=Washington State University Vancouver|date=2021-06-09|accessdate=2024-02-26 |language=}}</ref> This is a digital museum dedicated to reviving and maintaining these works to make them accessible to all. Physical artifacts are held at the [[Electronic Literature Lab]] in [[Vancouver, Washington]], US.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Electronic Literature Lab |url=https://dtc-wsuv.org/electronic-literature-lab/index.html |access-date=2024-05-06 |website=dtc-wsuv.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-18 |title=Still booting after all these years: The people stuck using ancient Windows computers |url=https://www.bbc.com/future/article/20250516-the-people-stuck-using-ancient-windows-computers |access-date=2025-05-26 |website=www.bbc.com |language=en-GB}}</ref>

== History ==
This digital museum originally housed 30 separate collections of 2,500 [[electronic literature]] works<ref name=wsu/><ref>{{Cite web |title=A Tour of ELO's The NEXT {{!}} ELMCIP |url=https://elmcip.net/critical-writing/tour-elos-next |access-date=2024-02-24 |website=elmcip.net}}</ref> which had increased to over 3,000 works by 2022.<ref name=grigor>{{Cite book |last1=Grigar |first1=Dene |url=https://doi.org/10.48197/fot2022 |title=The Future of Text |last2=Snyder |first2=Richard |year=2022 |isbn=979-8367580655 |editor-last=Frode |editor-first=Alexander |volume=III |chapter=Metadata for Access: VR and Beyond |doi=10.48197/fot2022 }}</ref> The NEXT uses an Extended Electronic Metadata Schema (ELMS) to describe the complex and interactive digital works it holds. This metadata describes the work and alerts readers to potential reading issues such as fleeting text, color use, or requirements for moving a mouse or moving with a [[virtual reality]] environment.<ref name=grigor /> The lab opened officially in 2011.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Electronic Literature Lab |url=https://dtc-wsuv.org/electronic-literature-lab/history.html?fbclid=IwZXh0bgNhZW0CMTEAAR2QXgKjd6RfSZkvhPaAy_l9adXCsTfnLkOGrIk2mf8KRiYPW3FSzF0gFss_aem_Ae4Jgk4YUfD56xYz6TZ1FROCbP_FpW6eX-VbVNahAe2bRtGuY89E4Y6DzV6KA64Hzqy62Rlk3i6pkHVMbVuQowxt |access-date=2024-05-06 |website=dtc-wsuv.org}}</ref>

== Reviving works ==
Electronic literature pieces have used software available at the time that are since obsolete, such as [[HyperCard]], [[Eastgate Systems]]' StorySpace, Director, ToolBox, and Flash. Recreating works

The NEXT has re-created these works by migrating them to newer systems. The NEXT Museum has re-imagined many individual works, including:

* [[Charles Bernstein (poet)|Charles Bernstein]], ''An Mosaic for Convergence'' (1997 original publication, 2019 re-imagined)<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grigar |first=Dene |date=June 2020 |title=Maintaining Accessibility to Born-Digital Literary Art |url=https://thedigitalreview.com/issue00/index.html |journal=The Digital Review |issue=1}}</ref>
* [[Richard Holeton]], ''[[Figurski at Findhorn on Acid]]''<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Grigar |first=Dene |date=September 2021 |title=The Ethics of Digital Preservation: Obligation to Future Generations |url=https://thedigitalreview.com/issue01/index.html |journal=The Digital Review |volume=1}}</ref>
* [[Caitlin Fisher (artist)|Caitlin Fisher]], ''[[These Waves of Girls]]''<ref name=":2" />
* John McDaid,  ''[[Uncle Buddy's Phantom Funhouse]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last=Grigar |first=Dene |date=October 2023 |title=Reimagining Hypertexts |url=https://thedigitalreview.com/ |journal=The Digital Review |issue=3}}</ref>'' in 2021
* [[Stuart Moulthrop]], [[Victory Garden (novel)|''Victory Garden'']]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Grigar |first=Dene |title=Reconstructing Stuart Moulthrop's Victory Garden |url=https://thedigitalreview.com/issue02/index.html |journal=The Digital Review |volume=2}}</ref> in 2022
* [[David Kolb]], ''Socrates in the Labyrinth and Caged Texts''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Caged Texts |url=https://archive.the-next.eliterature.org/kolb/caged-texts/copy-v2/index.html |access-date=2024-02-25 |website=archive.the-next.eliterature.org}}</ref> in 2022
* Bill Bly, ''We Descend'' in 2023<ref>{{Cite web |title=We Descend, The Complete Edition |url=https://the-next.eliterature.org/ |access-date=2024-02-26 |website=The NEXT |language=en-us}}</ref>

=== Noting metadata ===
Where recreating the work is not yet possible, such as Shockwave works like Jim Andrew's [[Nio (electronic literature)|Nio]], and [[Noah Wardrip-Fruin|Noah Wardrip Fruin]] et al.'s ''[[The Impermanence Agent]],'' the NEXT has provided as much metadata as possible.

== Individual author collections ==
The NEXT Museum also focuses on collections for notable authors in the electronic literature field, which include their own digital works and other donated physical or digital materials. For example, the [[Marjorie Luesebrink|Marjorie C. Luesebrink]] Collection holds 66 works. Luesebrink created and published 27 of these works under the pen name M.D. Coverley—and the NEXT Museum re-imagined, migrated, and developed video playthroughs of these works as they were written on now-obsolete software. The other works in this collection were donated by Luesebrink and include her personal copies of other author's works.<ref name="reviewsindh.pubpub.org">{{Cite journal |last1=Lillvis |first1=Kristen |last2=White |first2=Melinda |date=2023-08-28 |title=Review: Marjorie C. Luesebrink Collection at ELO's The NEXT |url=https://reviewsindh.pubpub.org/pub/marjorie-c-luesebrink-collection/release/1 |journal=Reviews in Digital Humanities |language=en |volume=IV |issue=8 |doi=10.21428/3e88f64f.fb0bd342 |issn=2766-9297|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Online journal and publication collections ==
Online journals were founded by communities and individuals. The NEXT Museum has curated and collected works from these journals, including the [[The Iowa Review|Iowa Review]] Web (1999-2008)  BeeHive (1998 -2004), Cauldron and Net (1997-2002 founded by [[Claire Dinsmore]]), Poems That Go  (2000-2004), Turbulence.org (1996-2016 co-founded by [[Jo-Anne Green]]), and The New River (1996–present).<ref>{{Cite web |title=The NEXT Online Journals |url=https://the-next.eliterature.org/ |access-date=2024-02-26 |website=The NEXT |language=en-us}}</ref> These collections have a wider range than electronic literature, as the Turbulence collected online Portugeuese Netart from 1997-2004.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Online Portuguese Netart 1997 {{!}} 2004 |url=https://the-next.eliterature.org/ |access-date=2025-07-05 |website=The NEXT |language=en-us}}</ref>

== Academic publications ==
[[Stuart Moulthrop]] and [[Dene Grigar]] co-authored two works  to document The NEXT's Pathfinder project, which provided video and audio recordings of currently inaccessible works using historically appropriate platforms, termed "traversals":<ref>{{Cite web |last=culturalstudiesleuven |date=2018-07-02 |title=Traversals: The Use of Preservation for Early Electronic Writing |url=https://culturalstudiesleuven.net/2018/07/02/traversals-the-use-of-preservation-for-early-electronic-writing/ |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=Cultural Studies Leuven |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2018-07-01 |title=Review of Traversals: The Use of Preservation for Early Electronic Writing |url=https://leonardo.info/review/2018/07/review-of-traversals-the-use-of-preservation-for-early-electronic-writing |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=Leonardo/ISASTwith Arizona State University |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Challenges of Born-Digital Fiction: Editions, Translations, and Emulations: Cover of Dene Grigar & Stuart Moulthrop's Pathfinders |url=https://scalar.usc.edu/works/the-challenges-of-born-digital-fiction--editions-translations-and-emulations/cover-of-dene-grigar--stuart-moulthrops-pathfinders |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=The Challenges of Born-Digital Fiction: Editions, Translations, and Emulations: The Multimedia Accompaniment to the Print Edition |language=en}}</ref> ''Pathfinders: Documenting the Experience of Early Digital Literature'' (June 2015)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Project Description |url=http://dtc-wsuv.org/wp/pathfinders/description/ |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=Pathfinders |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Ortega |first=Élika |date=2016-02-23 |title=Preservation Paths. A Review of Pathfinders: Documenting the Experience of Early Digital Literature by Dene Grigar and Stuart Moulthrop |url=https://journals.psu.edu/dls/article/view/59747 |journal=Digital Literary Studies |language=en |volume=1 |issue=1 |doi=10.18113/P8dls1159747 |doi-broken-date=12 July 2025 |issn=2376-4228}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |title=Pathfinders: Introduction to Pathfinders |url=https://scalar.usc.edu/works/pathfinders/introduction |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=Pathfinders |language=en}}</ref> and ''Traversals: The Use of Preservation for Early Electronic Writing''<ref>{{Cite web |title=Traversals |url=https://mitpress.mit.edu/9780262035972/traversals/ |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=MIT Press |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |title=Traversals: The Use of Preservation for Early Electronic Writing | chapter=Foreword |url=https://academic.oup.com/mit-press-scholarship-online/book/30669/chapter-abstract/260280522?redirectedFrom=fulltext |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=academic.oup.com| date=7 April 2017 | publisher=The MIT Press | isbn=978-0-262-03597-2 }}</ref> (April 2017).

Cambridge University Press, Digital Literary Studies, has released Dene Grigar and Mariusz Pisarski's work: ''The Challenges of Born-Digital Fiction'' (March 2024), as a print work<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Grigar |first1=Dene |title=THE CHALLENGES OF BORN-DIGITAL FICTION: Editions, Translations, and Emulations |last2=Pisarski |first2=Mariusz |date=2024 |publisher=[[Cambridge University]] Press |isbn=978-1-009-18147-1 |doi=10.1017/9781009181488 |issn=2633-4380}}</ref> and as a multi-media online work.<ref>{{Cite web |title=The Challenges of Born-Digital Fiction: Editions, Translations, and Emulations |url=https://dtc-wsuv.org/wp/ell/2021/02/14/the-challenges-of-born-digital-fiction-editions-translations-and-emulations/ |access-date=2024-03-24 |website=Electronic Literature Lab |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book |last1=Grigar |first1=Dene |last2=Pisarski |first2=Mariusz |date=February 21, 2024 |title=The Challenges of Born-Digital Fiction: Editions, Translations, and Emulations |url=https://www.cambridge.org/core/services/aop-cambridge-core/content/view/D7C93C1C77F8ED920D86234E00AF1448/9781009507370AR.pdf/the-challenges-of-born-digital-fiction.pdf |doi=10.1017/9781009181488 |isbn=9781009181488 |issn=2633-4399}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Flor |first=Micz |title=Hypertext & Art, A Retrospective of Forms - Musei Capitolini, Rome, 2023 |url=https://mi.cz/art/20230906-Musei-Capitolini-Hypertext-and-Art.html |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=Home of Micz Flor |language=de}}</ref>

== Exhibitions ==
The NEXT Museum curates exhibitions, such as Vision Unbound for Women's History month (2024),<ref>{{Cite web |title=Vision Unbound |url=https://the-next.eliterature.org/exhibition/vision-unbound/ |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=the-next.eliterature.org}}</ref> Hypertext an art in Italy September 5–8, 2023 in conjunction with the ACM Hypertext Conference,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Hypertext and Art |url=https://the-next.eliterature.org/exhibition/hypertext-and-art/ |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=the-next.eliterature.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Hypertext and Art |url=https://the-next.eliterature.org/exhibition/hypertext-and-art/events.html |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=the-next.eliterature.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-09-06 |title=Christian Wachter (@ChristianWachter@fedihum.org) |url=https://fedihum.org/@ChristianWachter/111019401211945821 |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=FeDiHum |language=en}}</ref> and AfterFlash.<ref>{{Cite web |title=afterflash {{!}} Exhibit |url=https://the-next.eliterature.org/exhibition/afterflash/ |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=the-next.eliterature.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Afterflash |url=https://dtc-wsuv.org/preserving-electronic-literature/projects/afterflash.html |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=dtc-wsuv.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=These Waves of Girls - Caitlin Fisher |url=https://www.yorku.ca/caitlin/waves/ |access-date=2024-03-25 |website=www.yorku.ca}}</ref>
